title: Thyristor-pair sense amplifier: T-RAM's latch reborn as periphery
idea: Failure mined: T-RAM died because a thyristor used as the storage cell had temperature-dependent holding current and standby leakage. Fix: use a cross-coupled gated-lateral thyristor pair as the bitline sense amplifier instead of the 6-8 transistor latch. It is biased only for the ~5 ns of sensing, so holding-current drift and standby leakage never matter, and its regenerative pnpn gain resolves ~20 mV in one step.
why: Periphery (fact 7): the sense-amp stripe is ~10-15% of the die. Two devices per bitline pair instead of 6-8 shrink it ~50-60% (~6% of die area back), and the higher gain tolerates a smaller cell signal.

title: Latching vertical-thyristor sub-wordline drivers from Kilopass VLT
idea: Failure mined: Kilopass's vertical layered thyristor (VLT) DRAM was abandoned over cell variability and the lack of a fab partner. Fix: use the VLT device where variability is harmless, as the sub-wordline driver. One anode pulse latches it on to drive the 3 V wordline and a cathode pull resets it, so each driver is a single ~4F^2 vertical device with no static decoder hold state.
why: Sub-wordline driver and local decoder strips are ~8-10% of the die. A vertical latching driver cuts them ~3x and removes static hold power, giving back ~5-6% of die area.

title: Time-to-latch sensing rescues Z-RAM floating-body margin
idea: Failure mined: Innovative Silicon's Z-RAM read the parasitic bipolar current of a floating body, and the 0/1 current difference shrank below sense-amp offset at 32 nm. Fix: read the delay until the parasitic BJT latches under a fixed bias ramp. That delay depends exponentially on stored body charge, and a time-to-digital converter shared by 16 bitlines digitizes it.
why: Turns a few-uA current difference into a multi-ns timing difference (~10x effective margin). That makes capacitorless cells (no 70:1 capacitor, fact 1) readable at scaled nodes, and sharing the TDC keeps periphery small.

title: Same-age reference cells let the sense threshold follow leakage decay
idea: Failure mined: resistance drift ate Optane's PCM read window until drift-tracking reads were added. Fix for DRAM: every row carries 4 reference cells written with 1s and 0s in the same activation as the data. At read they are charge-shared onto the reference bitline, so the threshold falls in step as stored 1s leak instead of sitting fixed at VBL/2.
why: Refresh (fact 3): a decaying 1 stays above an equally decaying midpoint for longer, roughly 2-3x the usable retention. That cuts refresh energy and bandwidth loss 50-65% for ~0.5% array overhead.

title: Lock-in AC tone read buries memristor sneak currents
idea: Failure mined: HP's TiO2 memristor crossbar died on sneak-path currents and line leakage that swamped the selected cell. Fix: put a small 200 MHz tone on the selected wordline only, hold all other lines at AC ground, and read the bitline through a mixer and integrator locked to that tone. DC bias leakage, half-select currents and 1/f noise all fall outside the detection band.
why: Selectorless 1k x 1k tiles can be read with >30 dB rejection of the background. That removes selector layers and makes tiles 4-16x larger, so decoders and sense amps take a smaller share of die area.

title: Second-harmonic polarization read makes FeRAM non-destructive
idea: Failure mined: Ramtron FeRAM's read switched the ferroelectric, causing fatigue and imprint and forcing a write-back on every read. Fix: apply a sub-coercive sine (~0.2 Vc) and detect the phase of the second harmonic of the displacement current with a phase-sensitive sense amp. The nonlinear permittivity is asymmetric, so the harmonic's sign follows the polarization direction without switching it.
why: Removes destructive read and restore energy (fact 8, ~5.9 pJ per useful bit) and read-induced fatigue, pushing ferroelectric cells toward unlimited read endurance.

title: Chain DRAM: Toshiba's chain-FeRAM topology with linear capacitors
idea: Failure mined: Toshiba's chain FeRAM (each capacitor in parallel with its transistor, 16 in series) died with Toshiba's FeRAM exit and its plate-pulse complexity. Fix: build the chain with ordinary DRAM linear capacitors. To read cell k, turn off only its transistor so its capacitor sits in series between the chain and the bitline; one bitline contact serves 16 cells and no plate pulsing is needed.
why: 16x fewer bitline contacts cut bitline capacitance ~40%, which raises the signal. Bitlines can then be 1.5-2x longer with proportionally fewer sense amps, and the cell gets denser without contacts.

title: PLEDM gain-cell current lets 2048 cells share one sense amp
idea: Failure mined: Hitachi dropped its PLEDM gain cell (a vertical multi-tunnel-barrier transistor on a storage gate) when it exited DRAM. The overlooked strength was a current output that does not depend on bitline capacitance. Fix: hang 2048 PLEDM-style cells on one bitline with a current-integrating, auto-zeroed sense amp, instead of the 256-512 cells per charge-sharing bitline today.
why: Cuts the sense-amp count 4-8x (SA stripe from ~10-15% of the die to ~3%) and removes the bitline-capacitance limit on cell charge.

title: Nantero's nanotubes as BEOL periphery transistors, not memory cells
idea: Failure mined: Nantero NRAM stalled on CNT-fabric switching variability. Fix: use aligned CNT films as BEOL CNFETs made below 400 C. A wide device averages over hundreds of tubes, so variability only has to meet logic-level tolerance. Row predecoders, column muxes and secondary sense stages are then built above the capacitor array.
why: Periphery is ~49% of the die (fact 7). Moving even half of it over the array gives ~1.3-1.4x more bits per wafer with no new EUV layers, using a domestic, tungsten-free device stack.

title: Tezzaron's split periphery fixed with in-array 16:1 preamp multiplexing
idea: Failure mined: Tezzaron's DiRAM moved sense amps onto a separate logic die but was capped by TSV pitch and lack of capital. Fix: give each bitline a 2-transistor gain preamp in the array wafer and time-multiplex 16 preamps onto one 1 um hybrid bond. Latching, write-back and ECC run on a bonded logic wafer from a mature U.S. node.
why: The array wafer becomes ~85-90% cells vs ~51% today (fact 7), ~1.7x bits per array wafer. The periphery wafer uses cheap non-EUV logic, which lowers blended capital intensity.

title: HMC's SerDes replaced by sense amps driving TSVs directly
idea: Failure mined: Micron's Hybrid Memory Cube lost on SerDes power and cost. Fix: each bank's secondary sense amps drive their TSV with a 100-150 mV charge-domain swing straight to a strobed latch on the base die. This deletes the DRAM-side global I/O lines, data buffers, serializers and DQ drivers.
why: Data-movement energy (fact 5): ~0.5-1 pJ/bit vs 3-4 pJ/bit for HBM, and ~8-10% of the DRAM die's periphery is deleted.

title: ThruChip inductive links tucked under the sense-amp stripe
idea: Failure mined: Keio's ThruChip inductive coupling and Samsung's Wide I/O both died, coils on area cost and TSVs on yield cost. Fix: lay the coupling coils in spare top metal directly over sense-amp stripes and arrays, beat crosstalk with code-division multiplexing among neighboring coils, and receive with sense-amp-style clocked latches. Data then crosses 8-12 thinned dies with no signal TSVs, only power vias.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): removing signal TSVs and their keep-out zones recovers part of the ~3x area-per-bit penalty and the 20-30% yield loss, because failed dies can be swapped before final bonding.

title: Charge-trap-trimmed sense amps: offset fixed once, transistors minimum size
idea: Failure mined: MRAM ventures such as Spin Memory could not shrink their arrays because low-TMR signals needed huge low-offset sense amps (offset scales as 1/sqrt(area)). Fix: put a nitride charge trap in each sense-amp input transistor's gate stack and program it at wafer test, with field recalibration, to null the offset. SA devices can then be minimum size, and the same trick works for DRAM sense amps.
why: Halves to quarters SA area, or lets the cell signal fall ~3x for a smaller capacitor (fact 1): ~5% of die area or a shallower capacitor.

title: Zero-extra-mask lateral bipolar sense amps from BiCMOS DRAM's ashes
idea: Failure mined: Hitachi's 1990s BiCMOS DRAM had superb bipolar sensing but died on extra masks and cost. Fix: form lateral npn transistors in the SA stripe from the existing buried-wordline trench, LDD and contact implants, with no new masks. The bipolar input pairs match Vbe to ~0.5 mV, ~10x better than MOS (5-10 mV).
why: The required bitline signal drops ~5x, so the storage capacitor can shrink ~3-5x (aspect ratio from 70:1 toward 20:1, fact 1) or bitlines can be ~3x longer with fewer SAs.

title: Avalanche-gain bitline preamp borrowed from failed impact-ionization MOS
idea: Failure mined: I-MOS (the impact-ionization MOSFET) died as a logic switch from high voltage and hot-carrier damage over billions of cycles. Fix: make a gated p-i-n avalanche preamp the first sensing stage, firing once per activation for ~1 ns and multiplying the cell's charge-share signal 10-30x before a conventional latch. Its duty cycle is ~1e-4 of logic use.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): cell capacitance can drop 5-10x (to ~0.5-1 fF), allowing planar or short capacitors and easing 3D DRAM (fact 2).

title: Resonant adiabatic wordline drive, reversible computing's missing killer app
idea: Failure mined: adiabatic and reversible logic (MIT, Younis) died because irregular logic needed multi-phase resonant power clocks. DRAM is the opposite case: wordlines and bitlines are large, regular capacitive loads switched on a periodic tRC beat. Fix: drive them from shared LC tanks with inductors in the package substrate, swinging to 3 V and back while recovering the charge.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): recovers 60-80% of wordline and bitline CV^2 energy, cutting activation energy ~2-3x without lowering any voltage.

title: Transient negative capacitance cancels bitline load only during sensing
idea: Failure mined: negative-capacitance FETs flopped because NC turned out to be hysteretic and stable only transiently. Fix: transient is all sensing needs. A thin HZO NC capacitor is switched in series with the bitline only for the ~3 ns charge-share window to partly cancel bitline capacitance, then disconnected before hysteresis matters.
why: The charge-share signal dV = Q/(Cs+Cbl,eff) grows ~2-4x, allowing ~2-3x smaller cell capacitors or 2x longer bitlines (half the SAs).

title: Automata Processor salvaged as a sense-amp key-match GET engine
idea: Failure mined: Micron's Automata Processor put state machines next to DRAM arrays and died on an alien programming model. Fix: add one XOR plus wired-NOR comparator per 64 sense amps and expose a single command, GET(key). A broadcast key is matched against every key in the open row (one hash bucket), and only the matching value leaves the chip.
why: Data movement (fact 5) and overfetch (fact 8): hash and key-value lookups move 64 B instead of 8 KB, ~100x fewer bits on the bus, for ~1-2% of SA-stripe area.

title: Resonant-capacitance read of varactor cells, after RCA's CED stylus
idea: Failure mined: RCA's Capacitance Electronic Disc read its signal as capacitance shifts in a 915 MHz resonant circuit, but its contact stylus wore out. Fix without contact: the storage node is the gate of a MOS varactor, and the cell is read by the resonant-frequency shift of a short bitline LC tank at a few GHz. The read draws no charge from the node, so no restore is needed.
why: Destructive read and restore (fact 8): removes write-back energy, so the same row can be re-read at ~1/3 the energy, and row-hammer exposure falls because reads stop disturbing neighbors.

title: Servo-marked racetracks: hard-disk servo loop fixes domain-wall shift errors
idea: Failure mined: IBM's racetrack memory stalled on pinning-induced over- and under-shifting of domain walls. Fix: interleave a known servo pattern every 32 bits. The read MTJ's sense amp time-stamps each domain-wall arrival, and a per-track controller trims the next current pulse width, like hard-disk servo wedges.
why: Pushes shift error rates from ~1e-4 toward ~1e-12, so one read head can serve hundreds of bits and sense amps are shared over ~100x more bits (fact 7).

title: Virtual Channel Memory reborn as BEOL shadow row buffers
idea: Failure mined: NEC's Virtual Channel SDRAM added SRAM channel buffers between the sense amps and I/O but died on area cost and standards politics. Fix: stack 4-8 extra row buffers as BEOL oxide-transistor 2T dynamic latches directly above the SA stripe, at zero silicon area, so each bank keeps several rows open.
why: Overfetch and activation (facts 8, 9): higher row-hit rates cut activations 2-3x, and activation energy and row-hammer exposure fall in proportion.

title: Periphery foundry shuttle: the DRAM fab access startups never got
idea: Failure mined: Z-RAM, T-RAM and Nantero each died partly because they could never prove their sensing or cells inside a real DRAM flow. Fix: a for-profit multi-project-wafer service on a U.S. DRAM pilot line that sells 1 mm^2 slots next to a standard array. Startups drop in new sense amps, decoders or cells and get silicon back in 10 weeks.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital intensity: a periphery experiment drops from ~$50M to ~$100k, and learning cycles run ~5x faster.

title: Royalty-free JEDEC array-to-periphery bonding standard
idea: Failures mined: RDRAM died in a royalty war and Gen-Z in consortium fragmentation. Fix: a JEDEC standard for the hybrid-bond interface between DRAM array wafers and periphery wafers (bond map, preamp electricals, test hooks), backed by a royalty-free patent pool. Any U.S. logic fab can then sell periphery wafers to any array maker.
why: Capital intensity and U.S. manufacturability: periphery (~49% of the die) moves to commodity logic fabs, cutting the capital needed to enter DRAM by ~30-40%.

title: Gigahertz CCD loops: one floating-diffusion amp per 64 bits
idea: Failure mined: 1970s CCD memories (Fairchild, Intel 2416) lost to DRAM on millisecond serial latency and charge-transfer loss. Fix: 64-stage buried-channel CCD loops with imaging-grade transfer efficiency (>99.9999%), 2-phase clocked at 4 GHz (worst-case 16 ns rotation), each sensed and re-injected by one floating-diffusion amplifier. Packets hold 2 bits (4 charge levels), and there are no per-bit contacts, capacitors or wordline drivers.
why: 10x at the same cost: ~2F^2 per packet vs 6F^2 (3x) x 2 bits per packet (2x) x periphery shrinking from 49% to ~10% (~1.7x) = ~10x. Built with CMOS-image-sensor masks (no capacitor module, little EUV) in U.S. image-sensor fabs.

title: Skyrmion bubble memory: globally clocked major/minor loops, TMR detectors
idea: Failure mined: magnetic bubble memory (TI, Intel Magnetics) died on micron-size bubbles, 100 kHz shifting and millivolt permalloy detectors. Fix: keep its best idea, one global drive that clocks every loop at once with no per-bit transistors, but use 25 nm skyrmions in Co/Pt multilayers pushed by a global spin-orbit current sheet. Data is read through block-replicate gates onto a major loop with one 200% TMR detector per 4096 bits.
why: 10x at the same cost: ~60 nm^2 per bit vs ~860 nm^2 per DRAM cell, with periphery amortized over 4k bits. The films are blanket sputtered layers with ~2 critical masks, no capacitors and no EUV.

title: Vertical NAND-structured DRAM strings with shadow-page sequential read
idea: Failure mined: Toshiba's 1993 NAND-structured DRAM put cells in series to eliminate contacts, but died because cells had to be read and restored in strict order. Fix: build 64-cell vertical strings in a 3D-NAND-style stack (word planes deposited and etched once, a thin capacitor at each tier) and treat each string as one burst. A shadow latch page in bonded periphery reads it out sequentially and restores it in reverse order.
why: 10x at the same cost: 64 tiers from one channel-hole etch (3D NAND cost structure, ~1 EUV layer), with one contact and one sense amp per string, give ~10-15x bits/mm^2 at similar wafer cost. A 64-bit string matches cache-line bursts.

title: Snapback counting reads N stacked threshold cells per crosspoint
idea: Failure mined: Optane died partly because each extra deck needed its own lithography and decoders, so cost never scaled past two decks. Fix: deposit 8 chalcogenide threshold-switching memory layers in series at every crosspoint, pattern them with one etch, and engineer a different threshold window for each layer. One voltage ramp per pillar is read by counting and timing the snapback current spikes, whose pattern encodes all 8 states.
why: 10x at the same cost: 8 bits per 4F^2 crosspoint vs 1 bit per 6F^2 is ~12x density, with one patterning step and one decoder set shared by all 8 layers, so decks no longer multiply masks.

title: Core-memory sense weaving cancels sneak current in selectorless 3D crosspoint
idea: Failure mined: core memory's sense wire zig-zagged through the cores so half-select noise cancelled, a trick lost in the move to semiconductors, while selectorless vertical crosspoints died on sneak current. Fix: pair each data pillar with a woven twin pillar that crosses the same word planes, with its half-selected cells biased in mirror image. A differential sense amp subtracts the matched sneak currents and leaves only the selected cell's current.
why: 10x at the same cost: without a selector, 32 deposited word planes stack under one pillar etch (4F^2 per tier, roughly 1.5 tiers' worth of patterning cost), ~10-20x bits/mm^2. The twin pillar doubles pillar count, not cost.

title: Single-electron electrometer sense amps make 300-electron cells readable
idea: Failure mined: Hitachi's room-temperature single-electron memory (Yano) died because the SET was too variable as a storage device. Fix: use the SET only as the sensor, a 3 nm silicon-island electrometer per 32-cell local bitline with charge sensitivity near 0.01 e, auto-calibrated on every access. Cells then need only ~300 electrons (~0.05 fF), which planar thin-film storage nodes can hold.
why: 10x at the same cost: a 100x smaller capacitor removes the 70:1 pillar and allows a 3D-NAND-style stack of 32+ tiers of lateral planar cells from deposited layers, ~10x bits/mm^2 at similar litho cost.

title: Zettacore redox molecules: eight built-in reference levels per cell
idea: Failure mined: Zettacore's porphyrin molecular memory stored charge in discrete oxidation states but died on CMOS process heat and slow voltammetric reads. Fix: after the 400 C steps, graft thermally robust ferrocene/porphyrin mixtures with 7 redox couples onto a nanoporous TiN electrode. The sense amp's reference ladder is a reference electrode coated with the same molecules, so the potential plateaus self-calibrate and each cell stores 3 bits.
why: 10x at the same cost: 3 bits per cell x a crosspoint-compatible 4F^2 footprint (the porous electrode supplies ~50 fF-equivalent charge) x fewer reference generators = ~9-12x vs 1 bit per 6F^2. The molecules cost pennies per wafer.

title: Selectron-style binary-coded tier selection replaces the 3D DRAM staircase
idea: Failure mined: RCA's Selectron tube picked one of 256 storage spots with combinations of a few grid bars, a decoder built into the medium, and died on vacuum-tube complexity. Fix: in a 3D DRAM stack, each tier's cells sit behind log2(N) series select gates whose thresholds are set by log2(N) masked implants, so 6 shared vertical gate lines decode 64 tiers. Staircase contacts and per-tier wordline drivers disappear.
why: 10x at the same cost: periphery and staircase area stay nearly flat as tiers grow (log N, not N), which moves 3D DRAM break-even from ~26 tiers to ~8 (fact 2) and makes 64-128 tiers ~10x denser at near-3D-NAND cost per mm^2.

title: 16-level DRAM via segmented-bitline capacitive-DAC successive approximation
idea: Failure mined: the 1990s multi-level DRAMs from Toshiba and NEC died because splitting ~150 mV into many levels destroyed margin and their staircase sensing was slow. Fix: split each bitline into binary-weighted segments that double as the capacitor DAC of a 4-step successive-approximation sense, trimmed per subarray against a stored reference charge, with one SAR comparator shared by 4 bitlines.
why: 10x at the same cost: 4 bits per cell in an open-bitline 4F^2 cell (6x vs 1 bit per 6F^2) x halved SA area from sharing (~1.5x) = ~9-10x, with no new process layers, only a periphery redesign.

title: Electron-beam-addressed charge film (EBAM) with field-emitter arrays
idea: Failure mined: 1970s EBAM/BEAMOS (GE, Control Data) stored bits as charge written and read by an electron beam on a MOS target, and died on vacuum, beam deflection and slow serial access. Fix: replace the deflected beam with a CMOS-driven Spindt field-emitter array in which each tip covers a 64x64 patch at 8 nm spot pitch through a small electrostatic microlens. Bits are charge in a nitride film, read by beam-induced current to a common backplate.
why: 10x at the same cost: no per-bit access transistor, wordline or bitline. An 8 nm bit pitch on an unpatterned film is ~13x DRAM density, and the only patterning is the emitter array at a relaxed ~200 nm pitch (no EUV).

title: Hadamard-coded multiplexed reads solve vertical ReRAM's sneak network
idea: Failure mined: vertical ReRAM (VRRAM) from Samsung and SanDisk stalled because sneak paths and IR drop worsened with every added plane. Fix: read all 64 cells of a pillar together with 64 measurements under Hadamard-coded +/- bias patterns on the word planes, then invert the known resistor-network model in a small periphery ASIC to recover each conductance. As in Hadamard spectroscopy, this gains ~sqrt(64) in SNR over one-at-a-time reads.
why: 10x at the same cost: 64 deposited planes per pillar etch become usable (VRRAM's whole premise) with ~8x SNR to spare, ~15x bits/mm^2 vs DRAM at 3D-NAND-like cost per mm^2. Latency is amortized because a pillar's 64 cells are read together.

title: Plated-pillar magnetic memory: coincident-current writes, inductive non-destructive reads
idea: Failure mined: plated-wire memory (UNIVAC, Apollo era) read magnetic bits non-destructively with no per-bit transistor but died on hand-assembled wire. Fix: build it monolithically by ALD-coating vertical pillars with a soft magnetic film inside a stack of deposited word planes. Coincident currents in a plane and a pillar write one intersection, and a plane pulse rotates the film so the pillar picks up an inductive or AMR signal without erasing the bit.
why: 10x at the same cost: a transistorless 4F^2 cell per tier and 32 tiers from one hole etch, with unlimited magnetic endurance and no refresh, ~15x bits/mm^2. Periphery scales per plane and per pillar, not per bit.

title: Vernier decoders address sub-lithographic spacer wires, learned after fab
idea: Failure mined: the HP and Caltech nanowire/molecular crossbars died because nothing could address 5 nm-pitch wires from 50 nm-pitch lithography. Fix: pattern array lines by quadruple spacer pitch-splitting to ~6 nm half-pitch, and cross them with coarse gate lines drawn at a slightly different pitch so each coarse pair coincides over exactly one fine wire, like a vernier scale. A power-up calibration records the actual coincidences in a small remap table.
why: 10x at the same cost: the array reaches ~6 nm half-pitch with zero EUV (spacers are cheap depositions), (12/6)^2 = 4x, times 1.5x for a 4F^2 crosspoint and ~1.7x for decoders that stay at coarse pitch, ~10x bits per cost.

title: DSA arrays made defect-tolerant by sense-amp-level remapping
idea: Failure mined: directed self-assembly lithography died in high-volume manufacturing because it could not pattern irregular periphery or hit the ~0.01/cm^2 defect target. Fix: once periphery moves to a bonded logic wafer, the array wafer is purely periodic, which is what block copolymers do well. Each sense-amp group carries a remap table filled at test, so DSA defects (~1/cm^2) are mapped out like bad columns.
why: 10x at the same cost: block copolymers at ~7 nm half-pitch with no EUV give (12/7)^2 = ~3x density, x1.9 from an all-array wafer, x1.5 from regular 4F^2 vertical-channel cells, ~9-10x at lower capital.

title: Row-granular decompressor in the sense-amp stripe, after IBM MXT
idea: Failure mined: IBM's MXT compressed main memory died on decompression latency and a costly controller far from the DRAM. Fix: put a wide, row-granular decompressor (zero-run coding plus 4-bit quantization tables for AI weights, KV caches and activations) right after the secondary sense amps. Its work overlaps the activation's tRCD and rows are stored compressed, so effective capacity multiplies with no added latency.
why: 10x effective density at the same cost for AI data: 4:1 quantization x ~2.5:1 sparsity and zero-run coding = ~10x usable capacity per bit cell. It also cuts data-movement energy (fact 5) ~10x per useful value, for ~3% of die area.

title: Plasma-display memory effect: global sustain waveform replaces refresh and transistors
idea: Failure mined: plasma displays held each pixel's state as wall charge under a global AC sustain waveform, with only row and column drivers and no per-pixel transistor, and lost to LCD and OLED on power. Fix: each crosspoint cell pairs a thin threshold switch with a small capacitor in a hysteresis loop. A global sustain clock re-pumps every 1 cell while 0 cells never fire, and coincident row/column pulses set or clear individual cells.
why: 10x at the same cost: no access transistor, refresh controller or refresh bandwidth. 4F^2 cells in 4 self-aligned decks sharing lines (~6x) x periphery shrinking to ~20% (~1.6x) = ~10x.

title: Delay-line regenerator: one fast sense amp services 64 dynamic bitlines
idea: Failure mined: mercury and magnetostrictive delay-line memories used one regenerating amplifier for thousands of bits and died only on serial access. Fix: in a 3D DRAM, the vertical bitlines hold their charge-shared signals dynamically for ~30 ns while one 20 GHz-class sense amp visits 64 of them through a fast mux, latching and restoring each in 0.4 ns. Row access stays random; only the sensing is serialized.
why: 10x at the same cost: SA area falls ~64x, so 3D DRAM breaks even at ~6-8 tiers instead of 26 (fact 2), and 48-64 tiers from shared etch steps give ~10x bits/mm^2.

title: 77 K memory pods: cold sensing permits flat capacitors and tiers
idea: Failure mined: the Microsoft-Rambus cryo-DRAM program was shelved because cooling general servers cost more than it saved. Fix: target AI clusters that already run liquid-nitrogen loops. At 77 K leakage falls by >1e6 (refresh nearly vanishes), kT/C noise and SA offset fall ~2-4x and bitline resistance falls ~6x, so a 0.4 fF planar MIM cell is enough and can be stacked in deposited tiers.
why: 10x at the same cost: replacing the 70:1 capacitor (fact 1) with flat cells allows 16-24 litho-shared tiers (~10x bits/mm^2). Cooling energy is offset by the eliminated refresh and lower I^2R losses.

title: Snap-through buckled-beam NEMS crosspoint: bistable, contactless, self-selecting
idea: Failure mined: the first-generation NEMS memories from Cavendish Kinetics and Nantero died on stiction and contact wear. Fix: a pre-buckled 40 nm nanobeam over each crosspoint snaps between two stable shapes without touching anything. Snap-through has a sharp voltage threshold, so half-selected cells never flip, and the state is read as differential capacitance to the row and column electrodes.
why: 10x at the same cost: transistorless 4F^2 cells with built-in selection, unlimited contactless endurance and zero leakage (no refresh). Four sacrificial-release decks sharing lines, plus minimal periphery, give ~10x bits per wafer cost.

title: Charge-injection-device cells: two-gate X-Y charge storage with non-destructive reads
idea: Failure mined: GE's charge-injection device (CID) imager lost to CCDs, yet it had an X-Y addressed, transistor-free pixel of two coupled MOS gates, read non-destructively by moving charge between the gates and sensing the column. Fix: use CID pairs as memory cells, with the row gate and column gate overlapping one storage well. A write injects charge; a read shifts it under the column gate and back, so the charge never leaves the well and can be re-read for multi-level sensing.
why: 10x at the same cost: a transistor-free ~4F^2 cell (1.5x) x 3 bits per well from averaged non-destructive re-reads (3x) x no restore and much less periphery (~2x) = ~9-10x, using planar CMOS-image-sensor processing.

title: Write-once AI weights move to a 3D antifuse ROM tier
idea: Failure mined: Matrix Semiconductor's 3D one-time-programmable diode/antifuse memory was dense and cheap but found no market for write-once bits. Fix: frozen inference weights are exactly that market. Program them into 8-deck 3D antifuse crosspoints with a DRAM-class read path (short bitlines, 40 ns random read), freeing HBM and DRAM for KV cache and activations.
why: 10x at the same cost: 8 decks x 4F^2 = ~12x DRAM bits/mm^2 with no capacitor, refresh or write path. Weights are 50-80% of inference DRAM demand, so the DRAM bought per deployed model falls 2-5x.

title: IBM eDRAM micro-sense-amps built inside each 3D DRAM tier
idea: Failure mined: IBM's deep-trench eDRAM, with 3-transistor micro sense amps on 32-cell local bitlines, died only because GlobalFoundries quit 7 nm. Fix: carry the micro-SA into 3D, with a 3-transistor thin-film micro-SA beside each 16-cell lateral bitline in every tier. Each tier becomes a self-sensing short-bitline array, where a 1 fF planar capacitor still yields ~100 mV.
why: 10x at the same cost: short local bitlines remove the capacitor bottleneck that blocks 3D DRAM (fact 2), and 32-48 tiers of lateral planar cells from shared etches give ~10x bits/mm^2 at ~3D-NAND cost.

title: 1T-8C ferroelectric stack: plate-line selection and twin-plate reference sensing
idea: Failure mined: Ramtron's FeRAM never shrank because each bit needed its own transistor (1T1C, often 2T2C). Fix: stack 8 HZO capacitors vertically on one access transistor's storage node, each on its own plate line, and read one by pulsing its plate while the other 7 float. A twin dummy plate provides a matched reference that cancels coupling from the unselected capacitors on the shared node.
why: 10x at the same cost: 8 bits per transistor on a ~4F^2 vertical-channel footprint = ~12x bits/mm^2, with all 8 capacitors made from one deposition stack and one hole etch.
